newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, U.S. discuss joint anti-drug fight - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France, U.S. discuss joint anti-drug fight - Chirac.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac said on Monday the United States and France were discussing a new joint crusade against iillegal drugs.
"We must move up a gear," he said.

In a two-hour television interview devoted to the problems of young people, Chirac said narcotics problems were "taking on extremely serious proportions" in France. And he said half the drugs in the world were consumed in the United States.
Speaking of cooperation between Washington and Paris, he said: "We are discussing to see how one could very strongly relaunch the struggle against drugs from the lowest level to the biggest mafias."

He also said he had asked France's centre-right government to work out a three-year plan to "considerably raise the means for fighting drugs." Use of hard drugs in France was rising more than other types, he said.
Chirac also renewed French criticism of liberal drug policies in the Netherlands, where modest amounts of soft drugs are sold at so-called "coffee shops".
"Liberalisation has failed everywhere, including in Holland," Chirac said.

The Netherlands, current holder of the European Union presidency, has been at odds with France for years over drugs policies. According to Dutch statistics, the Netherlands has 1.6 addicts per 1,000 head of population against about 2.5 per 1,000 in France. REUTER
